notes: NO ONLINE CATALOGUE EXISTS. laopala.in is a corporate/brand marketing site with zero e-commerce: no product listing pages, no product detail pages, no prices, no cart, no search, and therefore no site-reported count anywhere. Zero rows is the correct answer here, matching the c24 (HomeGoods) / c26 (Kirkland's) no-catalogue precedent (status ok + rows []). ACCESS: plain direct fetch, HTTP 200, no bot protection, no WAF, no Rule 2 route needed. robots.txt carries NO Claude-specific disallow (full contents: 'User-agent: *' + a single 'Disallow: /blog/bone-china-crockery-elegance-redefined'), so the Amazon-India-style opt-out precedent does not apply. LANGUAGE: renders natively in English (html lang="en"); no Hindi/regional category names encountered, so no translation was required. RULE 3 IDENTITY CHECK PASSED - this is the genuine corporate storefront of the listed company, not a reseller: footer reads 'La Opala RG Limited, Eco Centre, 8th Floor EM-4, Sector-V, Kolkata - 700091, West Bengal, India', and /investors serves a full SEBI Regulation 46 investor-relations section (quarterly results through FY 2025-2026, annual reports 2020-21 onward, board-meeting intimations up to 6th August 2026, shareholding pattern, credit rating, code of conduct). STRUCTURAL VERIFICATION THAT NO CATALOGUE IS SERVED, not inferred: (1) the full mega-menu was extracted from the rendered header markup - its entire product-side navigation is 'Our Brands' -> 4 brand pages (Diva, La Opala, Solitaire Crystal, Cook Serve Store Borosilicate) -> 11 design-line collection pages (Classique, Ivory, Cosmo, Pearl, Quadra, Sovrana, Velvett, Tea & Coffee, Novo, Storage, Bakeware); the only other top-level items are About, Gifting Elegance, Media, Investors, Blog, Contact. (2) All 16 of those brand/collection pages were fetched and parsed: each is prose marketing copy plus a lifestyle image slideshow plus a 'Download Brochure' PDF link plus a 'Find us here' block linking out to Amazon.in, Flipkart and Zepto. (3) Grep across all 19 saved pages found zero 'add to cart', zero class="product"/data-product attributes, zero rupee symbols and zero 'N products/items/results/designs/pieces' count phrases (the only 'Rs.' hits were a false positive inside the string 'careers.php'). (4) Nine candidate catalogue routes probed - /products, /product, /shop, /search, /catalogue, /store, /collection, /collections, /api/products - all HTTP 404. (5) No sitemap.xml, sitemap_index.xml or sitemap.php (all 404) and robots.txt declares no Sitemap. (6) No shop/store subdomain (shop.laopala.in and store.laopala.in both fail to resolve). (7) Page JS is only jquery.min.js, slick.min.js, app.min.js and reCAPTCHA - a static jQuery/slick marketing build with no SPA product API. Retail sale is entirely third-party (Amazon.in, Flipkart, Zepto, Myntra), which is out of scope for this brand-site row. WHY NO ROWS WERE EMITTED EVEN AS STRUCTURE: the site's product-side navigation consists exclusively of brand pages and design-line 'Collections', both of which are on the brief's NEVER EXTRACT list (Collections, Brands, brand listing pages). There is no product-type tree anywhere on the site - no 'Dinner Sets', 'Bowls', 'Plates', 'Glassware' or equivalent nodes - so no in-scope leaf category exists to carry a qty. The only quasi-product-type labels are 'Tea & Coffee' (presented as one of the eight Diva design collections, not as a type node) and 'Storage'/'Bakeware' under Cook Serve Store Borosilicate, which are excluded anyway as food-storage containers and bakeware. The per-collection image slideshows (7 to 30 unique photos each, each rendered twice as main slider plus thumbnail strip) are lifestyle gallery images, NOT product tiles - they carry no product name, no link and no ID - so they were deliberately NOT counted as qty; doing so would have been an inferred count, which the one rule that matters forbids. SCOPE NOTE for the merge: had a catalogue existed, in-scope lines would have been Diva and La Opala opalware dinnerware plus Solitaire Crystal glassware/barware/vases (filed under Kitchen & Dining per the brief), while the Cook Serve Store Borosilicate brand (cookware, bakeware, food-storage containers) and the 'Gifting Elegance' page (gift guide) would have been excluded. As expected for this manufacturer, the site's own navigation confirms there is no lighting and no mirrors range at all - the company makes only opalware, crystalware and borosilicate glass.
